To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel framework to solve the problem of spatial crowdsourcing in the presence of many workers, which is much faster and scalable than the previous approaches, and at the same time, generates high quality results.

(i) the existing solutions to spatial crowdsourcing are not optimal when multiple workers are considered, (ii) a 3-phase approach is able to generate high quality solutions, (iii) the 3-phase is very slow and not scalable, and (iv) a Bisection framework is able to achieve high quality results in a scalable manner

1) the 3-phase matching-scheduling framework is the best solution for the problem of matching tasks and scheduling workers for spatial crowdsourcing; 2) however, this framework does not scale to a large number of workers; and 3) the Bisection framework scales to a large number (e.g., 100,000) of workers, but it is not the optimal solution.
